# PLAN — iteration 2
## Current state assessment
The incumbent is timing-feasible at 7 LUTs and 9 FFs, so iteration 2 must strictly reduce LUTs to improve the objective. Iteration 1 passed behavior and timing checks but used 10 LUTs after narrowing the counter and relying on natural wrap; it was rejected. Top numeric latency is unknown, so no numeric annotation is required.

## Hypothesis
Restoring an explicit 8-bit terminal-count reset may map more compactly than iteration 1’s natural-wrap counter, potentially returning to the baseline LUT count while preserving the same 8-bit state and registered output behavior.

## Instruction for generator
Keep `counter` as an 8-bit register, but replace iteration 1’s unconditional modulo increment with an explicit `counter == 8'hff` branch that sets it to zero; otherwise increment by one. Preserve the synchronous reset and `pwm_out <= (counter < {24'd0, duty})` update exactly. This is an area experiment: promote only if all gates pass and routed LUTs are strictly below 7; matching 7 LUTs is not an objective improvement.
